baseline_platform_feedback: docs/fts_42598_feedback.json; 42.598 points associated with f73f785 by submission order, not this candidate
implementation: Store the current ID datum pointer beside each small posting head score, pass those datums to the same initialized comparator, and remove per-comparison iterator-index lookup. Pointer ownership and lifetime remain with its token iterator.

query_microbenchmark.validation: All 500 outputs per group checked against CN8001 / EN11000 / mixed7332 / LIMIT20.

original_sql_benchmark.reason_for_followup: Old mixed query was unusually slow in all three groups of primary baseline round 2; LIMIT also changed direction. Both concerns were retained and triggered a reversed pair.
original_sql_benchmark.diagnostic_statistics: All original report means and all 126 samples retained. Pooled nine-group-per-version medians are additional diagnostics, not replacements for original means or platform metrics.

method.process_cpu_clock: Whole-process utime+stime including background threads; /proc/PID/stat at 100 Hz.

profiling.workload: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fts_large_bench.docs WHERE MATCH(title_en,content_en) AGAINST('database performance audit');

initial_incomplete_sampling.correction: The earlier early-workload-exhaustion explanation was not supported. The client completed only 3413 full responses before termination; do not claim all 20000 requests finished. Initial samples contain idle/background frames and the old sampler skipped unknown new thread IDs. Exact cause of each idle snapshot is unconfirmed.
initial_incomplete_sampling.rerun: Preserve initial artifacts; use a longer workload, assert client liveness and refresh the GDB thread map to capture 100 samples.

profiling.caveat: Paused GDB snapshots are qualitative. Initial 40 captured samples include idle/background frames and are preserved but excluded from primary bottleneck counts. Earlier attribution to workload exhaustion was unsupported and is corrected in the sampling notes. Rerun asserts a live longer workload and refreshes GDB thread IDs.

original_sql_benchmark.anomaly: All three old mixed-query groups in sql_baseline_2 were much slower. They remain included in every mean/median. A reversed B A follow-up was predeclared after observing this; pooled sample medians are diagnostic and do not replace original report means or platform metrics.

correctness.scope: Existing 26 cases cover cached-ID refill lifetime, stream exhaustion, reuse, one through four words, visible IDs/scores, Boolean and numeric filters, prepared execution, rollback, partitions, sparse vectors and AI integration. No new golden outputs or modified expectations.
correctness.native_ps_protocol: Earlier extra --ps-protocol failures on both versions remain unpassed, not rerun. Normal-protocol SQL PREPARE/EXECUTE is covered by passing cases.

adoption_decision.supporting_evidence: CN/EN/mixed micro wall improves 4.06%/10.35%/9.46%, CPU improves 4.59%/10.74%/9.92%. Primary original SQL CN/EN means improve 6.65%/10.34%; reverse follow-up improves CN/EN/mixed 5.53%/10.22%/10.11%.
adoption_decision.anomalous_evidence: Primary old mixed round 2 is 3.9520 ms (3.7664-4.2491 ms groups), inflating the primary mean improvement to about 27%; do not claim that as a source-only gain. All rows remain in every aggregate.
adoption_decision.negative_evidence: Original LIMIT is slower in primary pair 2 and reverse follow-up (follow-up 0.52% slower). No stable LIMIT gain is claimed, even though micro and pooled medians are positive.

limitations: Two primary runs and one follow-up run per version; shared host without exclusive CPU or frequency control.
Original reports print the modified checkout HEAD 0e103cf for both executables. Immutable binary paths, SHA-256 and patch identity establish provenance.
Unchanged SELECT 1 and tokenization timings also improved; do not attribute their gains or the entire query differences to this source change.
Pooled medians describe all samples including anomalies. They are not used to edit benchmark reports, scoring formulas, inputs or test expectations.
No full reload or build speed experiment was run for this query-only implementation.
No platform score is inferred; 42.598 remains the preceding source feedback.
Previously documented binary-PK projection, native PS and earlier rejected-trial limitations are unchanged.
